property_summary: Calling Deposit with a positive msg.value should not revert (i.e., always succeed) when called on a freshly initialized caller.
If Deposit is called with a positive Ether value, the call must not revert (i.e., succeed) when the caller's previous recorded balance in C is at least as large as the deposit amount.
If Deposit is called with a positive Ether amount and the caller's prior on-chain recorded balance (observable via public getter) is at least the amount, then Deposit must not revert.
Calling Deposit with value v should never revert when the caller's previous recorded balance is 0 and v > 0 (original increases balance, mutant would underflow and revert).

In the reference, performing Deposit() (including via receive) always increases the caller's balances[msg.sender] by the sent msg.value (so after a Deposit and then a successful Collect the recorded balances for any address never goes below the net of historical deposits minus collects), whereas the mutant that subtracts on Deposit can make balances decrease on Deposit and thus can cause balances(key) after a Collect call to differ (be lower) for some inputs.

For any caller A, after funding A (via Deposit/receive) and then calling Collect(x) from A to withdraw ≤ balance, the contract's public balances for every address K remain >= 0 and in particular for the caller A the balances[A] after Collect equals prior balances[A] - x (i.e. collecting cannot increase any balance); the mutant that subtracts on Deposit can make balances for some address decrease unexpectedly so there exists fuzzed inputs where balances(address) after Collect differs (is lower) between reference and mutant, violating the non-increase rule for the withdrawer.

For any caller who is the recipient of a successful Collect(amount) call, the reference preserves non-negativity and reduces that caller's recorded balances by exactly the collected amount (so balances[recipient] after Collect equals balances[recipient]_before - amount and never becomes negative); the mutant that subtracts on Deposit can make balances for some address go lower after Collect, breaking this invariant for some fuzzed inputs.

For any caller who deposits some Ether and then calls Collect(n) (with n ≤ their recorded balance), the reference contract guarantees that after Collect the caller's recorded balances equals its prior balance minus n (i.e., Collect deterministically reduces the caller's own balance by exactly the withdrawn amount); the mutant (which subtracts on Deposit) violates this for some fuzzed inputs causing the recorded balance after Collect to differ.

For any caller who has funded the contract (via Deposit/receive) and then calls Collect(x) with x ≤ balances[caller], the reference contract always reduces that caller's public balances by exactly x (balances[caller]_after == balances[caller]_before - x); the mutant that subtracts on Deposit can cause balances to be lower beforehand and thus makes balances[caller]_after differ for some fuzzed inputs, so the property is violated.
